semantic_review: The original common mock accepts connections serially, consumes the entire per-connection request queue, and closes after that queue. Splitting queues into one request per connection permits the next phase handshake without changing this common implementation.

The client determines reuse from its serialized connection compatibility projection or transport closure. When identity differs it awaits a new handshake before replacing the old connection, so the serial mock's wait for another old-socket request is a source-supported blocking mechanism.

The projection retains sandbox, sandbox_mode, workspaces and tool inventory. The pinned submit_turn helper explicitly requests PermissionProfile::Disabled. The revised audit does not falsely collapse all possible changes to workspaces or claim a captured compatibility-projection trace.

These tests assert metadata-free prewarm and fresh Git workspace metadata after repository mutation. They do not assert a socket-reuse contract. Retaining the same ordered event expressions and selecting the last follow-up at [2][0] / [3][0] preserves that purpose.

The new [1,1,1] / [1,1,1,1] assertions constrain request cardinality and delivery, while all original workspace values, root-turn assertions, waits and tool arguments remain exact. The fixture deliberately closes each one-request socket; these counts are fixture behavior, not evidence that production identity naturally changes on every request.
limitations: No native execution, Rust invocation, source edit, or dynamic connection-identity trace was performed in this independent review.

The original three failure blocks support stopping at prewarm; source analysis explains a reachable transport/mock incompatibility. Exact projection fields/timing in each failed ephemeral case remain uncaptured.
Acceptance here is static review of the narrow fixture correction. Native original strict and full Core gates are still required.
